messages:
alex: Heads-up — running into a gap on per-API-key controls for internal services. We have a few infra keys (deploy agent, metrics-forwarder) that need higher short-term burst but we don't want permanent full-exempt status. Looking for proposals on safe semantics.

maria: +1. My take: offer a 'tiered key' model instead of binary exempt/non-exempt. Each key gets a base cap, a burst allowance window, and a daily budget. Admins can grant temporary top-ups that auto-expire. Keeps telemetry sane. :thinking:

srinivas: Telemetry question: how do we surface when a key is consuming burst quota vs base? We need clear metrics so cost owners can see token-level delta. Otherwise ops will be blind.

jules: Console UX idea: show a small timeline sparkline per key with two thresholds: base and burst. Hover shows 'burst used X / Y' and history of top-ups. Button to request temporary top-up that opens a changelist.

alex: sounds good. Important: default behavior for internal keys should be strict (base cap low) to prevent accidental high-cost loops. Top-ups require SRE approval and expire.

maria: Policy sketch (example):
```json
{
  "key_id": "service-deploy-agent",
  "base_rps": 5,
  "burst_tokens": 10000,
  "burst_window_secs": 60,
  "daily_budget_tokens": 200000,
  "auto_expire_topup": true
}
```
This keeps rate limiting at runtime cheap (leaky-bucket) and bursting controlled by tokens.

srinivas: Implementation note: leaky-bucket per key + long-term quota checkpointing in PG. For telemetry, emit metrics: `key.base_rate_used`, `key.burst_tokens_used`, `key.topup_events`. All tags: org, key_owner, service_tag.

sam: Rollout plan: 1) opt-in dev keys -> gather metrics 2) enforce for internal infra keys (non-prod) 3) canary for a small set of prod infra keys with manual top-up path 4) full enforcement with automatic block + contact info.

jules: Also add a small 'appeal' flow in console: if a team gets blocked, they can request immediate short-lived top-up (approval slack modal to SRE). That reduces pager noise.

alex: Agree. One more constraint: partner/third-party keys must never be allowed top-ups without legal/security review. Internal services only.

maria: Agreed. We'll add allowlist flag `can_auto_topup: true|false`. Partners default to false.

quota-bot: system: Rate limit snapshot for key service-deploy-agent at 2026-11-12T14:02:34Z: base_rate=5rps, burst=10000 tokens, burst_used=820, daily_used=42100. No action required. :white_check_mark:

srinivas: Nice — that snapshot format is helpful. Add a `recent_spikes` small array to the telemetry feed to detect repeated topup patterns.

alex: Question about billing: do temporary top-ups get charged to the owner's org or to a central infra bucket? We should default to owner's org for transparency, but offer billing-exempt infra keys with strict audit trail.

maria: Proposed: default charge to owner org. We support a `billing_override` flag for infra keys that routes cost to a central account; changes require 2 approvers and are auditable.

sam: On enforcement behavior: prefer soft-block first (429 + warning header + contact) for two weeks before hard-block to avoid prod outages. Track number of soft-blocks as signal for escalation.

jules: UX: show soft-block banner in console with one-click request top-up and link to docs. Also show last 7 days of soft-blocks in key details.

alex: OK. Action items: Maria drafts a formal policy doc + JSON schema for key tiering. Srinivas adds the telemetry metrics to the schema. Jules wires the console mockups. Sam writes the rollout runbook with canary list. I'll coordinate approvers for billing-exempt keys.

maria: I'll drop the initial policy draft into /docs/internal/key-tiers.md and ping eng-policy channel when ready.

srinivas: I'll stub the metrics and a lightweight exporter. Expect PR by EOD Friday.

sam: I'll own the runbook and canary list. Will schedule a short sync with SRE.

alex: Thanks all. If anyone else has edge cases (cron jobs, long-polling sockets) call them out here.

maria: Cron jobs: recommend lower base_rps + scheduled window to perform bulk work (timeboxed burst) to avoid constant bursting. Documented in draft.

jules: Long-poll sockets: treat as separate connection limit, not token-based. We'll add guidance in UX copy.

alex: Perfect. Close for now — we'll reconvene after PRs land. :v:
